newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, bellies end sharply up on spec buying.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, bellies end sharply up on spec buying.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures ended solidly higher, with hogs rallying on heavy speculative buying while pork bellies rallied on firm cash, CME floor traders said.
"The (pork) product market is firm, they're calling cash higher tomorrow (Thursday), why shouldn't we be higher?" one trader said.
Firm to higher calls for Thursday's cash hog markets generated additional speculative buying around midday and helped to push hog futures to triple-digit gains, floor traders said.
Cash hogs in key Midwestern markets were expected to trade steady to $0.50 cwt higher as packers attempt to gather enough hogs to put together a large Saturday slaughter, cash sources said.
Cold, windy weather in the northern Corn Belt was also said to have capped hog marketings and boosted futures.

Some of the day's gains were said to be commission house short covering instead of fresh buying, pit sources said. Dean Witter and local traders were short covering, and Merrill Lynch was an early seller in December hogs, traders said.
Traders said they see strong resistance in December hogs at 55.20 cent.
Commodity funds were said to be short the hog market, and a cluster of buy-stop orders was thought to be resting near 55.25 cent in December hogs, pit sources said.

Activity in pork belly trading was said to be moderate. The market's strength was attributed to the sharp gains in hogs, a smaller-than-expected out-of-town warehouse figure and firm cash markets, floor traders said.

On Tuesday, the CME reported a net-in movement of 1.143 million lbs of frozen pork bellies into warehouses outside Chicago, which compared with livestock analysts' range of estimates from 1 million to 2 million lbs.
December hogs settled up 0.550 to 1.000 cent per lb, with December up 0.900 at 54.950 cents and February up 0.925 at 74.950 cent.
February pork bellies settled up 1.15 cent at 70.550, with other months up 0.925 to 1.150.
